itinerary.title: Pickup and Transfer to Murchison Falls (via Ziwa Rhinos)
itinerary.description: Very early in the morning around 7:00 am, your guide/driver will pick you up and proceed to Murchison Falls National Park, located in the North Western part of Uganda, about 300 Kms from Kampala. On your way, you will visit the Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary in Nakasongola district, the home of Uganda's rhinos. Here, you will see white rhinos in their natural environment up close, providing an unforgettable experience. You will have a chance to see them on foot with a ranger guide for a maximum of one hour, taking as many photos as you can. After tracking, proceed to the Ziwa Rhino restaurant for lunch. Thereafter, drive to Murchison Falls National Park—the source of happiness for nature lovers. You will be welcomed by many olive baboons lined along the road. On arrival, visit the top of the falls to enjoy the breathtaking views and the great sound as the water squeezes through a narrow gorge of only 7 meters wide, dropping 43 meters into a pool with a lovely, thunderous sound. After 30 minutes at the falls, cross the River Nile to the Northern sector and check in at Parkside Safari Lodge for dinner and overnight.

itinerary.title: Early Morning Game Drive & Nile Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: Wake up very early for breakfast and set out for a morning game drive. Starting early provides a better chance of sighting species like lions, leopards, spotted hyenas, and jackals while they are still active before returning to their hideouts. You will also see elephants, buffaloes, giraffes, and birds like the Northern Red Bishop, Woodland Kingfisher, and African Paradise Flycatcher. After 5 hours, return to the lodge to relax and have lunch. At 1:00 pm, proceed to the River Nile for an afternoon boat cruise. This cruise offers an array of wildlife sightings, including Nile crocodiles, hippos, and lizards. As you cruise towards the bottom of the falls, you will encounter many huge Nile crocodiles. After 3 hours on the Nile, return to the landing site to meet your guide and head back to the lodge for dinner and overnight.

itinerary.title: Return to Kampala
itinerary.description: On this day, wake up early, pack your luggage, and have breakfast before embarking on your journey back to Kampala. You will enjoy a stopover for a hot lunch on the way. After lunch, proceed to Kampala, reaching in the evening, where your unforgettable 3-day safari comes to an end.

inclusions: 4x4 Safari Land Cruiser with Pop-up roof

itinerary.title: Flight to Murchison Falls & Nile Delta Cruise
itinerary.description: Pick up from Kampala or Entebbe and transfer to Entebbe airport (between 10 to 40 minutes approx.) for your scheduled flight with Aerolink to Pakuba/Murchison Falls NP at 12:30. Arrive at 13:30, where you will be met by the lodge's 4x4 safari van and transferred to the lodge for lunch. In the afternoon, we will take a Nile Delta cruise to Lake Albert—a paradise for bird watching. Keep a keen eye out for the rare Shoebill Stork if lucky. Return to the lodge for a relaxing evening.

itinerary.title: Morning Game Drive & Boat Cruise to the Bottom of the Falls
itinerary.description: Set out for an early morning game drive on the northern bank of the River Nile. Look out for elephants, lions, Cape buffaloes, Rothschild's giraffes, hartebeests, Oribi, spotted hyenas, and the elusive leopard. Return to the lodge for breakfast and lunch. In the afternoon (14:00), take a boat cruise upstream to the 'Bottom of the Falls'. Stop a few meters from the 'Devil's Cauldron' to witness the Nile squeezing through a 6-meter canyon with a thunderous roar. Spot hippos, crocodiles, and diverse bird species like the Goliath heron and Kingfisher along the 17km stretch. Disembark for a guided 1.5-hour hike to the 'Top of the Falls' for breathtaking views. The lodge car will pick you up from the top for the transfer back.

itinerary.title: Final Game Drive & Flight Back to Entebbe
itinerary.description: After breakfast, enjoy one last morning game drive in the wilderness before being transferred to Pakuba airfield for your scheduled flight with Aerolink to Entebbe at 13:45. Arrive at 16:30 to connect to your departure flight.

itinerary.title: Pickup and Transfer to Queen Elizabeth NP
itinerary.description: You will be picked up by the company driver-guide. After the briefing with the guide, our 3-day safari in Queen Elizabeth National Park begins in a 4x4 safari van. The amazing journey to Queen Elizabeth National Park — also known as the 'Medley of Wonders' — starts heading towards the west of the country. A stop-over can be made at the Uganda Equator at Kayabwe for taking photos, the famous water experiment, and easing yourself. You will then proceed to Mbarara City, the biggest city in Western Uganda, for an en-route lunch, and then proceed to Queen Elizabeth NP, reaching the lodge in the evening for check-in and relaxation.

itinerary.title: Game Drive in Kasenyi Plains & Kazinga Channel Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, the guide will take you to the park for a game drive in the Kasenyi plains in search of various animals. Nature is unpredictable — whatsoever mother nature gives us is what we receive from her. The drive will also take you to the crater lake Bunyampaka where you can even buy some souvenirs for yourself. After here, you will go back to the lodge for lunch. After lunch you will embark on a boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel, which connects the two lakes Edward and George, for various animals and birds. On a good day, large herds of elephants are spotted on the river bank, hippos, crocodiles, and various water birds which are permanent inhabitants of the channel. After the boat cruise, enjoy a game drive as you go out of the park back to the lodge for relaxing and overnight.

itinerary.title: Twin Crater Lakes Visit and Return to Kampala/Entebbe
itinerary.description: After morning breakfast, you will check out of the lodge and drive through the beautiful rolling hills of Rubirizi district. Rubirizi is blessed with a number of crater lakes; out of these you will be able to make a stop-over at the twin lakes in Kichwamba — also known as the 'Lakes in Love' — for photography and scenic views. You then proceed towards Kampala with an en-route lunch in Mbarara City. After lunch you will proceed back to Entebbe for your flight back home. The trip is over!

itinerary.title: Transfer to Bwindi Impenetrable Forest NP
itinerary.description: You will be picked up by the company driver-guide. After the briefing with the guide, our 3-day primate safari begins in a 4x4 safari jeep. The amazing journey to Bwindi Impenetrable Forest National Park — also known as the Gorilla Trip — heads towards Kabale and Kisoro in South-Western Uganda. A stop-over can be made at the Kayabwe Equator for taking photos and the famous water experiment. You then proceed to Mbarara for an en-route lunch, and proceed to Bwindi through the beautiful sceneries of Kabale and Rubanda, reaching the lodge in the late evening for dinner and overnight.

itinerary.title: Gorilla Trekking in Bwindi Forest
itinerary.description: After an early morning breakfast, you will drive to the park headquarters for briefing and registration of gorilla tracking. You will be given a packed lunch box and 1.5 litres of water, then drive to the park headquarters. On arrival, your guide will ask for your passport and gorilla permits to register and allocate you to a gorilla group. You will then wait for a briefing from the ranger guide. After the briefing you will be given your gorilla group and go for trekking — the activity takes between 3 to 4 hours depending on the gorillas' location. Once you find them, you will spend one magical hour with the gorillas taking photos. After that, you will go back to the starting point for certificate rewards, then drive back to the lodge for relaxing, dinner, and overnight.

itinerary.title: Batwa Community Visit & Return to Entebbe
itinerary.description: After an early morning breakfast, you will go and visit the Batwa (Pigmy) community for one hour, experiencing their traditional way of life and forest survival skills. You then embark on the journey back to Entebbe with an en-route lunch. After lunch, drive back to Entebbe. The end of a truly unforgettable trip!

Arrive in the Kibale Forest area in the afternoon and check in to your lodge. In the evening, attend an orientation briefing by your guide covering rules, safety, and what to expect during the chimp trekking adventure.

itinerary.title: CHIMPANZEE TREKKING & BIGODI WETLAND WALK

Enter the forest with your UWA ranger, following vocalisations and tracks to locate habituated chimp communities. Spend a magical hour observing them at close range. You may also encounter 12 other primate species, including red-tailed monkeys and black-and-white colobus. In the afternoon, take a guided walk through Bigodi Wetland Sanctuary to spot over 200 bird species (like the Great Blue Turaco), sitatunga antelopes, and otters. Conclude with a community village walk to meet local Batoro people and visit craft markets.

Optionally, embark on a cycling adventure through the Mpanga Tea Estate with scenic crater lake views. Depart Kibale mid-morning for the return drive. Enjoy an en-route lunch in Fort Portal or Mbarara and make a memorable photo stop at the Uganda Equator monument to straddle two hemispheres. Arrive in Kampala/Entebbe by early evening for drop-off at your hotel or the airport.

itinerary.title: KAMPALA/ENTEBBE – EQUATOR – MPAMBIRE DRUM VILLAGE – LAKE MBURO NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, your driver/guide will pick you up from Kampala or Entebbe at 7:00–7:30 am for the approximately 3–4 hour drive westward to Lake Mburo National Park. The route takes you through the towns of Mpigi, Masaka, Lyantonde and Kiruhura, passing through Uganda's lush green countryside of banana plantations, rolling hills and small rural trading centres. Keep an eye out for the distinctive long-horned Ankole cattle grazing beside the road — a symbol of western Uganda's rich pastoral culture.

En route, stop at Mpambire Drum Makers' Village — a fascinating cultural stop where you can watch local artisans hand-craft traditional Ugandan drums from cowhide and select timber. The craft has been passed down through generations and the village supplies drums to the entire country, including to the royal courts of Uganda's kingdoms. Browse the workshop and pick up a handmade souvenir if you wish.

Continue to the Uganda Equator monument at Kayabwe — the point where the road crosses the 0° latitude line. Stop for photographs, pick up souvenirs from the craft stalls and watch the fascinating water-flow experiment that demonstrates the Coriolis effect on either side of the Equator. A quick snack or refreshment break here before the final leg to the park.

Arrive at Lake Mburo National Park through Nshara Gate — and enjoy a game drive through the park en route to your lodge, as the tracks pass through prime wildlife territory. Lake Mburo is Uganda's smallest savannah national park, covering 370 km², yet it packs an extraordinary variety of wildlife into its acacia woodlands, open savannah, rocky outcrops, seasonal swamps and lakeshores. Check in to your lodge and enjoy a relaxed lunch.

After lunch, head to the jetty for a 2-hour afternoon boat cruise on Lake Mburo — the largest of the park's five lakes. The boat follows the eastern and southern shores of the lake, bringing you close to large schools of hippos wallowing in the shallows and Nile crocodiles basking on the banks. The lakeshores are a birdwatcher's paradise — with over 315 recorded species, look out for African fish eagles, malachite kingfishers, African finfoot, grey crowned cranes, papyrus gonoleks, blue-headed coucals and a variety of herons and egrets. The boat cruise also offers beautiful views of the surrounding savannah hills and acacia canopy.

Return to shore and head out for a late afternoon game drive through the park's open grasslands and acacia woodland. This is an excellent time to spot zebras, impalas, topis, Defassa waterbucks, warthogs, Cape buffaloes, bushbucks and olive baboons. Lake Mburo is the only national park in Uganda where you can see impalas and Burchell's zebras, and also one of the best parks for seeing the giant eland — Africa's largest antelope species. With a little luck, you may also spot a leopard resting on an acacia branch in the evening light. Return to the lodge at dusk for dinner.

Optional evening activity: Night game drive (additional cost) — a 2-hour guided drive after dark in search of nocturnal wildlife including leopards, hyenas, porcupines, genets, bushbabies and the occasional serval cat.
itinerary.stay: Mihingo Lodge (Luxury) / Rwakobo Rock (Mid-range) / Eagle's Nest (Budget)

itinerary.title: MORNING GAME WALK & GAME DRIVE – SALT LICK – RETURN TO KAMPALA/ENTEBBE
itinerary.description:
Rise early for a cup of coffee or tea before heading out at 6:45 am for a morning guided nature walk inside the park — one of the most distinctive features of Lake Mburo, as it is the only national park in Uganda where walking safaris are permitted within the park boundaries. Accompanied by an armed Uganda Wildlife Authority ranger, explore the park on foot through acacia woodland and open grassland, getting close to wildlife in a way that is simply not possible from a vehicle.

The early morning walk offers excellent opportunities to spot zebras, impalas, warthogs, topis and giant elands grazing as the nocturnal animals return to their dens. Birds are particularly active at this hour — listen for the call of the African fish eagle and watch for lilac-breasted rollers, red-faced barbet, Abyssinian ground hornbill and numerous sunbird species in the flowering acacias. The walk also takes you close to the lake, where you may spot hippos returning from their overnight grazing on the grasslands.

Return to the lodge for a full cooked breakfast and check-out. Before departing the park, stop at the salt lick — a natural mineral deposit near the lake where wildlife, particularly zebras, buffaloes and elands, gather to lick the salt-rich soil. This is a superb spot for close-up wildlife photography in a relaxed setting. Also stop at Rubanga Forest — a small but beautiful patch of tropical forest within the park that is excellent for forest birds and the occasional primate sighting.

Optional morning activity: Horseback safari — a truly unique way to experience Lake Mburo, riding through the savannah alongside zebras and antelopes. Available for all levels, from beginners to experienced riders (additional cost).

Depart Lake Mburo in the late morning and begin the return drive to Kampala or Entebbe International Airport. Stop at the Uganda Equator for a final photograph and lunch at a roadside restaurant en route. Continue through Masaka and Mpigi, arriving in Kampala or Entebbe by early evening. Drop-off at your hotel or the international airport for your onward flight.

itinerary.title: KAMPALA/ENTEBBE – MABIRA FOREST – JINJA – MBALE – SIPI FALLS
itinerary.description: Depart from your hotel at 7:00 am for the 5–6 hour drive eastward. Travel through the lush Mabira Forest, keeping an eye out for grey-cheeked mangabeys and red-tailed monkeys. Cross the River Nile at Jinja and continue through the rice and sugarcane plantations of Iganga. Stop in Mbale, the gateway to Mount Elgon, for lunch. After lunch, climb steadily into the Kapchorwa highlands through terraced hillsides of Arabica coffee and banana plantations tended by the Sabiny people. Arrive at Sipi village in the late afternoon and enjoy an evening stroll to a nearby viewpoint for your first glimpse of the falls cascading down the mountain.

itinerary.title: SIPI FALLS FULL HIKE – COFFEE TOUR – SEBEI CULTURAL EXPERIENCE
itinerary.description: Embark on the full Sipi Falls hike, visiting three distinct waterfalls: the Upper Falls (100m) with a hidden cave, the Middle Falls (85m) with its natural rock amphitheatre, and the spectacular Main Falls (75m). The hike takes 3–4 hours through community farms with views of Lake Kyoga. In the afternoon, enjoy a guided Arabica coffee tour—from bean to cup. Learn the process of picking, pulping, drying, and roasting the famous Bugisu AA coffee over an open fire. Conclude the day with a visit to the Sebei Cultural Centre to learn about the traditions and adulthood initiation ceremonies of the Sabiny people.

itinerary.title: MOUNT ELGON NATIONAL PARK – KAPKWAI FOREST EXPLORATION CENTER – MOUNTAIN HIKE
itinerary.description: Transfer to Kapkwai (2,050m) and meet your UWA ranger guide. Mount Elgon is an ancient extinct shield volcano with the largest volcanic base in the world. Choose between the Chebonet Falls Loop (3 hours), the Bamboo Forest Loop (5 hours) through giant lobelias, or the challenging Tutum Cave Trail (9 hours) where elephants visit to lick mineral salts. All trails pass through regenerating forest zones alive with 300+ bird species, including the endangered lammergeier. Return to the lodge in the afternoon for rest or optional rock climbing.

Visit Tewei Hilltop for 360-degree views of the valley. Optional: Stop at the ancient Nyero Rock Paintings in Kumi district (red ochre Stone Age art) en route to Kampala. Return through Mbale and Jinja, arriving in Kampala or Entebbe by early evening.

itinerary.title: NYAKALENGIJA (1,646m) – NYABITABA HUT (2,652m) | TREK DAY 1
itinerary.description:
Elevation: 1,646m → 2,652m | Distance: 9 km | Hiking Time: 5–6 hours

Transfer to the Nyakalengija trailhead. Meet your team: lead guide, assistant, cook, and Bakonzo porters. Enter the montane rainforest, climbing through dense vegetation draped in hanging mosses. Watch for L'Hoest's monkeys and listen for wild chimpanzees. Over 200 bird species are present, including the Rwenzori turaco. Arrive at Nyabitaba Hut, perched on a ridge above the Mubuku and Bujuku River valleys, offering spectacular views of the mountains.

itinerary.title: NYABITABA HUT (2,652m) – JOHN MATTE HUT (3,414m) | TREK DAY 2
itinerary.description:
Elevation: 2,652m → 3,414m | Distance: 10 km | Hiking Time: 6–7 hours

Descend into the Bujuku River valley before a long climb through successive vegetation zones. Pass through the giant heather zone—ancient trees encrusted with silver-green moss—before entering the 'Lost World' of giant groundsels and lobelias. The trail crosses numerous boggy sections with boardwalks. Arrive at John Matte Hut (3,414m), situated above the cloud line with magnificent views back down the valley.

itinerary.title: JOHN MATTE HUT (3,414m) – BUJUKU HUT (3,962m) | TREK DAY 3
itinerary.description:
Elevation: 3,414m → 3,962m | Distance: 7 km | Hiking Time: 5–6 hours

Cross the Bigo Bog, a vast alpine marsh criss-crossed by boardwalks and surrounded by giant lobelias. Climb steeply through heather moorland to Lake Bujuku, a glacial lake at nearly 4,000 metres. The lake is surrounded by the dramatic rock faces of Mount Stanley, Speke, and Baker. Bujuku Hut is the base for admiring the permanent glaciers. Look for rock hyrax and the rare Rwenzori red duiker in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: BUJUKU HUT (3,962m) – HUNWICK'S CAMP / KIHARO HUT (3,147m) | TREK DAY 4
itinerary.description:
Elevation: 3,962m → 3,147m | Distance: 9 km | Hiking Time: 5–7 hours

Climb initially through a lobelia swamp before ascending a rocky river bed to Hunwick's Pass. Enjoy extraordinary views of Kitandara Lake and the high peaks. Descend through towering heather trees and enormous moss-covered boulders into the Nyamwamba Valley. The route follows the river, passing spectacular mossy waterfalls. Arrive at Kiharo Camp in the early afternoon.

itinerary.title: KIHARO HUT (3,147m) – NYAKALENGIJA (1,646m) – KASESE – KAMPALA/ENTEBBE
itinerary.description:
Elevation: 3,147m → 1,646m | Distance: 14.6 km | Hiking Time: 6–7 hours descent

A satisfy descent through the full length of the Nyamwamba Valley, dropping 1,710 metres. Pass Lake Mahoma and re-enter the lush montane rainforest. Upon arrival at Nyakalengija, enjoy a traditional Bakonzo farewell song—a moving way to mark the end of the trek. Transfer to Kasese for a hot shower and lunch before the drive back to Kampala, arriving in the late evening.

In the late afternoon, enjoy a game drive through the Narus Valley—a permanent water source where wildlife concentrates in extraordinary numbers. Spot large elephant herds, Cape buffaloes, giraffes, zebras, and elands. Kidepo is Uganda's premier park for predator sightings—scan the rocky outcrops for lions and the open plains for the rare cheetah, spotted hyena, and black-backed jackal.

itinerary.title: KAMPALA – FORT PORTAL – RWENZORI ESCARPMENT – SEMULIKI NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description:
Depart from your hotel in Kampala at 7:00 am for the approximately 5–6 hour drive westward to Semuliki National Park via Fort Portal. The road follows the Kampala–Mubende–Fort Portal highway—the shorter and more scenic of the two western routes—passing through rolling hills, tea estates, and the rising foothills of the Rwenzori Mountains. Stop in Fort Portal for lunch with views of the peaks on clear days.

After lunch, descend dramatically off the Rwenzori escarpment toward Bundibugyo—one of the most breathtaking drives in Uganda. The road drops nearly 1,000 metres in elevation with sweeping panoramic views of the Semliki Valley and the distant blue hills of the DRC. Thatch huts shaded by West African oil palms begin to appear as you enter a landscape belonging to Central Africa. Arrive at Semuliki National Park, the easternmost extension of the great Ituri Forest of the Congo Basin. In the late afternoon, enjoy a game drive through the open savannah on the fringes of the park, spotting forest buffaloes, Uganda kobs, and elephants. The Semliki River boundary is home to large pods of hippos and massive Nile crocodiles.

itinerary.title: SEMPAYA HOT SPRINGS – FOREST NATURE WALK – BATWA CULTURAL VILLAGE – LAKE ALBERT BOAT CRUISE
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, set out for the Sempaya Hot Springs. The nature trail winds through lowland rainforest where you may see red-tailed monkeys and black-and-white colobus. Semuliki holds 441 bird species, including 46 Guinea-Congo biome species found nowhere else in East Africa. itinerary.title: KAMPALA/MBALE – SOROTI – MOROTO TOWN – MOUNTAIN BASE CAMP ORIENTATION
itinerary.description:
Depart from Kampala or Mbale in the early morning for the long but scenic drive northeastward to Moroto town — the capital of the Karamoja region and the gateway to Mount Moroto. The drive from Kampala takes approximately 9–11 hours; from Mbale approximately 5–6 hours via Soroti and Katakwi. An alternative for those with tight schedules is a chartered flight to Moroto Airstrip, which takes approximately 1.5 hours from Entebbe.

The drive itself is part of the adventure. As you leave behind the lush green farmlands of eastern Uganda and pass through Soroti — the gateway to the north — the landscape begins to transform dramatically. Red laterite soils replace the dark loam, sorghum and millet fields replace banana plantations, and the vegetation thins into open acacia-dotted savannah. Cattle herders in traditional Karamojong dress — ochre-stained shukas, elaborate bead necklaces and wooden walking sticks — drive their long-horned cattle along the roadside. This is one of Uganda's most culturally distinct and visually striking landscapes, and the drive sets the tone perfectly for the adventure ahead.

Continue through Katakwi and Napak, passing the dramatic inselberg of Mount Napak rising from the plains, before arriving in Moroto town. The great bulk of Mount Moroto — 3,083 metres of ancient volcanic rock rising sheer from the semi-arid Karamoja plains — dominates the skyline to the east of the town. Check in to your accommodation in Moroto and enjoy a warm meal.

Late afternoon: guided orientation walk around Moroto town with your local guide. Visit Moroto market — one of the most colourful and authentic markets in Uganda — where Karamojong and Tepeth traders sell beaded jewellery, gourds, traditional tools, sorghum beer and dried meats. Your guide will help you interact with community members and begin to understand the social structure, traditions and day-to-day life of the Karamojong people — one of East Africa's last remaining semi-nomadic pastoralist cultures. Purchase any final food supplies and fill water containers for the mountain. Briefing with your mountain guide on the route, safety and what to expect on the climb.
itinerary.stay: Karamoja Safari Camp / Kara-Tunga Guesthouse / Moroto Hotels (Budget)

itinerary.title: KODONYO TRAILHEAD – NADUKON VALLEY ASCENT – IMAGIT PEAK RIDGE CAMP (WILD CAMPING)
itinerary.description:
Elevation: ~1,200m (trailhead) → ~2,700m (ridge camp) | Distance: 10–12 km | Hiking Time: 5–7 hours

Rise early for breakfast and final preparations before transferring approximately 12 km by vehicle from Moroto town to the Kodonyo trailhead — the starting point for the ascent of Mount Moroto via the Nadukon Valley route. Meet your local Tepeth guide and porters at the trailhead. A short community introduction is made here — the trailhead sits near a Tepeth settlement and it is customary to greet the elders before entering the mountain.

The trail begins at the base of the mountain through classic Karamoja arid thorn savannah — flat-topped acacia trees, euphorbia candelabra cacti and dry red soil. The first section is a gradual ascent up the Nadukon Valley, following a rocky seasonal river bed flanked by increasingly dense vegetation. The temperature at the base can reach 35°C by mid-morning, so an early start is essential. Carry a minimum of 3 litres of water per person — there are natural springs on the mountain slopes but water should always be purified.

As you gain altitude, the dry savannah gradually gives way to dry montane woodland — a zone of denser trees, flowering shrubs and shade that provides welcome relief from the heat below. This is the habitat of the mountain's remarkable birdlife: over 220 species have been recorded on and around Mount Moroto, including the rare Doherty's bushshrike, Karamoja apalis (endemic to this region), Jackson's hornbill, Abyssinian roller, Heuglin's francolin and several species of sunbird and weaver. Look out also for vervet monkeys, rock hyrax, baboons and — if you are very fortunate — the elusive golden cat in the upper forest zones.

The upper section of the trail involves a fairly steep and at times rocky scramble — some sections require the use of hands on the steeper rock faces (no technical equipment required). The terrain becomes increasingly dramatic as you approach the main ridge line, with views expanding steadily behind you across the vast Karamoja plains stretching all the way to the horizon. On a clear day you can see far into neighbouring Kenya.

En route, pass through one or more Tepeth settlements on the mountain slopes. The Tepeth (also known as the So people) are the original and ancient inhabitants of the Mount Moroto massif — a small and little-known ethnic group who retreated to the mountain centuries ago as the Karamojong pastoralists expanded across the plains below. They live in traditional stone-and-grass homesteads, practice subsistence farming on the mountain slopes using natural spring water for irrigation, and are renowned for their deep knowledge of medicinal plants and oral history. Your Tepeth guide will facilitate introductions and help you understand the community's way of life, beliefs and their special relationship with the mountain they call home.

Reach the ridge camp below Imagit Peak in the late afternoon — a broad flat area on the ridge with ample space for tents and extraordinary 360-degree panoramic views: the Karamoja plains spread below to the west, the higher peaks of Sokodek (3,083m) and Sogolomon visible to the north, and the hills of Kenya to the east. Set up camp as the sun begins to descend toward the horizon. Your cook will prepare a warm meal over a camp fire as the stars begin to appear — at this altitude, far from any light pollution, the Milky Way stretches from horizon to horizon in a spectacle that is simply impossible to describe. Sleep under canvas with the wind, the stars and the silence of one of Uganda's most remote and untouched landscapes.
itinerary.stay: WILD CAMPING on the Mount Moroto ridge (~2,700m)

itinerary.title: SUMMIT PUSH – IMAGIT PEAK (2,950m+) – DESCENT – RETURN TO MOROTO / KAMPALA
itinerary.description:
Elevation: ~2,700m (camp) → ~2,950m+ (Imagit Peak) | Distance: 4–6 km return | Hiking Time: 2–3 hrs summit + 3 hrs descent

Wake before dawn to watch the sunrise over the Karamoja plains — one of the most spectacular and unforgettable moments of the entire trip. The temperature at night on the ridge can drop to 8°C or below, so a warm layer is essential for the early morning hours. Enjoy a hot cup of coffee or tea around the campfire as the sky turns from black to deep orange to gold, and the vast plains of Karamoja gradually emerge from the darkness below. A moment of pure, unrepeatable magic in one of Uganda's most remote corners.

After a warm breakfast, break camp and make the final push to Imagit Peak — the most popular and most accessible of Mount Moroto's summits, and the third highest point on the massif. The trail from the ridge camp to the summit involves some light scrambling over rocky outcrops and through dense montane scrub before breaking out onto the exposed rocky summit area. From Imagit Peak the panoramic views across the Karamoja plains, the Kenyan border highlands and the higher Moroto peaks are breathtaking — on a clear morning the visibility can stretch for over 100 kilometres in every direction.

Spend time on the summit taking in the views, photographing the dramatic landscape and marking the achievement with your guide. Optional for the very fit: your guide can assess conditions and fitness for an attempt on the higher Sokodek Peak (3,083m — the true summit of Mount Moroto), which requires an additional 2–3 hours of challenging ridge trekking and scrambling from Imagit. Discuss this possibility with your guide at the start of the trek.

Begin the descent from Imagit Peak, retracing the ridge and then descending via the Nadukon Valley or an alternative southern route through Tapac village — a spectacular traverse of the mountain massif from west to east, passing through further Tepeth communities. The descent takes approximately 2–3 hours and brings you out at a different point on the mountain's lower slopes, from where your vehicle will collect the group.

Arrive at the base of the mountain in the early afternoon. Transfer back to Moroto town for a hot shower, a cold drink and a celebratory lunch. In the afternoon, begin the return drive to Kampala or Mbale, arriving late in the evening.

In Rwanda there are 10 habituated gorilla groups that can be viewed by tourists — each group is visited by a maximum of 8 people per day and the visit lasts one hour. The trekking can take 1 to 8 hours and climb to altitudes in excess of 7,500 feet. The terrain is rough and at times muddy, but the beauty of the forest makes it entirely worthwhile. Once the gorillas are located, all fatigue is forgotten — this experience is often described as the most profound natural history encounter in the world. *Optional flight (supplement applies): Transfer (approx. 2 hours) to Kihihi or Kisoro airstrip for your scheduled Aerolink flight to Entebbe connecting directly with your departure flight.

Queen Elizabeth park entrance and game drives
Crater Lakes walk in Fort Portal

testimonial.quote: The combination of chimps, huge elephants, and finally the majestic gorillas was perfectly paced. Uganda is truly the Pearl of Africa.
testimonial.author: Johannes V.
testimonial.headline: A Safari Masterpiece!

itinerary.title: ENTEBBE/KAMPALA – ZIWA RHINO SANCTUARY – MURCHISON FALLS NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: Depart at 7:00 am for Murchison Falls NP. Stop at Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary, the only place in Uganda to track wild Southern White Rhinoceroses on foot—a successful conservation project that has restored the species to Uganda. After lunch in Masindi, continue to Murchison Falls and visit the 'top of the falls' to witness the Nile forcing through an 8-metre rock cleft in a thundering cascade. Check in to your lodge for dinner.
itinerary.stay: Paraa Safari Lodge / Nile Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Murchison River Lodge (Mid-range) / Red Chilli Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: MURCHISON FALLS – MORNING GAME DRIVE – NILE BOAT CRUISE TO THE BASE OF THE FALLS
itinerary.description: Pre-breakfast game drive in the northern bank savannah to spot elephants, Rothschild's giraffes, lions, and buffaloes. After breakfast, board the park launch for a boat cruise to the base of Murchison Falls. The riverbanks host one of the world's highest concentrations of hippos and crocodiles. Disembark at the base and hike to the top for dramatic views before returning to the lodge.
itinerary.stay: Paraa Safari Lodge / Nile Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Murchison River Lodge (Mid-range) / Red Chilli Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: MURCHISON FALLS – BUDONGO FOREST CHIMPANZEE TREKKING – TRANSFER TO KIBALE
itinerary.description: Cross the Nile to Budongo Forest for a morning chimpanzee trekking experience along the 'Royal Mile' trail, home to mahogany trees and multiple primate species. After a packed lunch, begin a scenic 6–7 hour drive southward through the Albertine Rift escarpment and Fort Portal crater lakes region to Kibale Forest National Park, the Primate Capital of the World.
itinerary.stay: Primate Lodge / Papaya Lake Lodge (Luxury) / Kibale Forest Camp / Isunga Lodge (Mid-range) / Chimpanzee Forest Guesthouse (Budget)

itinerary.title: KIBALE FOREST – CHIMPANZEE TREKKING – BIGODI WETLAND SANCTUARY WALK
itinerary.description: Morning chimpanzee tracking in Kibale's ancient rainforest, home to 1,500 chimps and 12 other primate species. Spend one hour with a habituated community. In the afternoon, embark on the community-run Bigodi Wetland Sanctuary walk, famous for the Great Blue Turaco, sitatunga antelopes, and rare papyrus birds. Optional evening night walk to spot nocturnal pottos and bushbabies.
itinerary.stay: Primate Lodge / Papaya Lake Lodge (Luxury) / Kibale Forest Camp / Isunga Lodge (Mid-range) / Chimpanzee Forest Guesthouse (Budget)

itinerary.title: TRANSFER TO QUEEN ELIZABETH NATIONAL PARK – KASENYI PLAINS GAME DRIVE – KAZINGA CHANNEL BOAT CRUISE
itinerary.description: Drive southward to Queen Elizabeth NP, straddling the equator. Game drive in the Kasenyi Plains, the park's prime predator circuit, for lions and Uganda kobs. In the late afternoon, enjoy the 2-hour Kazinga Channel boat cruise, witnessing huge herds of buffalo and hippos at the water's edge in the golden evening light.
itinerary.stay: Mweya Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Enganzi Lodge / Ihamba Lakeside Safari Lodge (Mid-range) / Kazinga Channel View Resort (Budget)

itinerary.title: KYAMBURA GORGE CHIMP TRACKING – ISHASHA TREE-CLIMBING LIONS – BWINDI ARRIVAL
itinerary.description: Track chimpanzees in the 'Valley of Apes'—Kyambura Gorge, a sunken forest slicing through the savannah. After lunch, drive to the Ishasha sector to search for the world-famous tree-climbing lions. Continue into the Kigezi highlands and the mist-filled valleys of Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, arriving in the evening.
itinerary.stay: Mahogany Springs Lodge / Bwindi Lodge (Luxury) / Silverback Lodge / Chameleon Hill Lodge (Mid-range) / Buhoma Community Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: BWINDI IMPENETRABLE FOREST – MOUNTAIN GORILLA TREKKING – BATWA CULTURAL EXPERIENCE
itinerary.description: The safari peak: mountain gorilla trekking in Bwindi. Enter the UNESCO World Heritage forest to find your assigned family. Spend one profound hour with these gentle giants (sharing 98.3% human DNA). In the afternoon, meet the Batwa (Twa) pygmy people, the forest's original inhabitants, for a respectful cultural encounter involving traditional music, fire-making, and medicinal knowledge.
itinerary.stay: Mahogany Springs Lodge / Bwindi Lodge (Luxury) / Silverback Lodge / Chameleon Hill Lodge (Mid-range) / Buhoma Community Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: LAKE BUNYONYI RELAXATION – ISLAND CANOE CRUISE – RETURN TO KAMPALA/ENTEBBE
itinerary.description: Drive to Lake Bunyonyi, Africa's second deepest lake. Enjoy a traditional wooden canoe cruise between the 29 islands, including Punishment Island. Bunyonyi is bilharzia-free and safe for swimming. In the afternoon, begin the return drive to Kampala or Entebbe via the Equator monument, arriving in the late evening.

inclusions: Ziwa Rhino tracking & Batwa cultural visit
Bottled drinking water in the vehicle

itinerary.title: ENTEBBE – BOTANICAL GARDENS BIRDING – LAKE VICTORIA SHORELINE – MABAMBA WETLAND ARRIVAL
itinerary.description: Begin birding immediately at the Entebbe Botanical Gardens (est. 1898), targeting the Great Blue Turaco, African Grey Parrot, and various weavers. Explore the Lake Victoria shoreline for African Fish Eagles, Pink-backed Pelicans, and the Blue-breasted Bee-eater. Transfer to a hotel near Mabamba Bay for an evening briefing from your specialist birding guide.
itinerary.stay: Papyrus Guesthouse Entebbe / Boma Hotel Entebbe / Imperial Resort Beach Hotel

itinerary.title: MABAMBA SWAMP – SHOEBILL CANOE SEARCH – TRANSFER NORTH TO MURCHISON FALLS
itinerary.description: At dawn, board traditional canoes in Mabamba Bay for a silent search for the prehistoric Shoebill Stork (Balaeniceps rex). Mabamba is one of the most reliable sites in Africa for this vulnerable giant. Also target the Papyrus Gonolek and Blue-headed Coucal. In the afternoon, drive north toward Murchison Falls NP, with a potential stop at Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary for further wetland birding.
itinerary.stay: Nile Safari Lodge / Paraa Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Murchison River Lodge (Mid-range) / Red Chilli Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: MURCHISON FALLS – GAME DRIVE BIRDING – NILE BOAT CRUISE – BUDONGO FOREST
itinerary.description: Morning birding in the northern savannah for the Abyssinian Ground Hornbill, Saddle-billed Stork, and Denham's Bustard. Mid-morning, enjoy a Nile boat cruise to spot six kingfisher species and the African Skimmer. In the afternoon, bird the famous 'Royal Mile' in Budongo Forest, targeting the Chocolate-backed Kingfisher and the African Dwarf Kingfisher among giant mahogany trees.
itinerary.stay: Nile Safari Lodge / Paraa Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Murchison River Lodge (Mid-range) / Red Chilli Rest Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: TRANSFER TO KIBALE FOREST – EN ROUTE BIRDING – BIGODI SWAMP AFTERNOON WALK
itinerary.description: Drive south to Kibale Forest, stopping at the Fort Portal crater lakes for the African Finfoot and Great Blue Turaco. In the afternoon, walk through the Bigodi Wetland Sanctuary, a community-run paradise for the Papyrus Gonolek, White-winged Warbler, and multiple primate species.
itinerary.stay: Primate Lodge Kibale / Papaya Lake Lodge (Luxury) / Kibale Forest Camp / Isunga Lodge (Mid-range) / Chimpanzee Forest Guesthouse (Budget)

itinerary.title: KIBALE FOREST BIRDING – GREEN-BREASTED PITTA SEARCH – TRANSFER TO QUEEN ELIZABETH
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn search for the legendary Green-breasted Pitta, one of Africa's most sought-after sightings. Also target the African Green Broadbill and the Bar-tailed Trogon in the forest canopy. In the afternoon, drive to Queen Elizabeth National Park, birding the Kamwenge road corridor for the Rwenzori Turaco and Doherty's Bushshrike.
itinerary.stay: Mweya Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Enganzi Lodge / Ihamba Lakeside Safari Lodge (Mid-range) / Pumba Safari Cottages (Budget)

itinerary.title: QUEEN ELIZABETH – KASENYI PLAINS BIRDING – KAZINGA CHANNEL CRUISE – MARAMAGAMBO FOREST
itinerary.description: Birding the Kasenyi plains for the Martial Eagle and Yellow-throated Longclaw. Afternoon boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel—one of the highest concentrations of waterbirds in Africa—to spot the African Skimmer and various egrets. Conclude with a forest walk in Maramagambo to see the Egyptian Fruit Bat colony and its associated predators.
itinerary.stay: Mweya Safari Lodge (Luxury) / Enganzi Lodge / Ihamba Lakeside Safari Lodge (Mid-range) / Pumba Safari Cottages (Budget)

itinerary.title: BWINDI IMPENETRABLE FOREST – ALBERTINE RIFT ENDEMICS – RUHIJA BIRDING – RETURN
itinerary.description: The grand finale at Bwindi's Ruhija sector (2,300m), targeting the 23 Albertine Rift endemics. Search for the African Green Broadbill (Grauer's), Shelley's Crimsonwing, and Grauer's Warbler at Mubwindi Swamp. In the afternoon, begin the return drive to Kampala or Entebbe for your departure flight.

inclusions: Private 4x4 safari vehicle with pop-up roof

itinerary.title: Arrival in Entebbe / Kampala
itinerary.description: Arrival at Entebbe airport, meet and greet. Transfer (approx. 30 minutes) to the hotel in the outskirts of Kampala overlooking Lake Victoria. No meals included today.

itinerary.title: Kampala to Murchison Falls via Ziwa Rhinos
itinerary.description: Early breakfast, then depart to Nakitoma to Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary (approx. 3½ hours). Game walk to track the white rhinos. Proceed to Masindi for lunch at Court View Hotel. Continue to Murchison Falls National Park driving through a beautiful landscape. Arrive at the lodge, check in and relax.

itinerary.title: Murchison Falls Game Drive & Nile Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: Morning game drive in the northern bank of the river Nile looking out for elephants, Cape buffaloes, giraffe, hartebeests, and potentially lions or leopards. After lunch, take an afternoon boat cruise upstream to the 'bottom of the falls'. Stop a few meters from the 'Devil’s Cauldron' and marvel at hippos, crocodiles, and water birds. Disembark to hike to the 'top of the falls'. Our driver will pick you up from the top to return to the lodge.

itinerary.title: Murchison Falls to Fort Portal
itinerary.description: Drive to Fort Portal via Hoima in the breathtaking landscape of the Albertine western Rift Valley. This is a long drive (8–9 hours) with several stopovers for relaxation and sightseeing as we pass verdant countryside, traditional homesteads, and farms. Enjoy a packed/picnic lunch on the way. Check in and relax.

itinerary.title: Kibale Forest Chimp Tracking & Queen Elizabeth NP
itinerary.description: Early transfer to Kibale Forest NP (approx. 45 minutes) for a morning dedicated to searching for chimpanzees and other primates. After lunch, proceed to Queen Elizabeth NP / Peninsula sector (approx. 3½ hours) for an evening game drive around the volcanic craters of Katwe.

itinerary.title: Kasenyi Game Drive & Kazinga Channel Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: Early morning game drive in Kasenyi area within Queen Elizabeth NP looking out for lions, buffaloes, elephants, and large numbers of Uganda Kobs. After lunch at Mweya Safari Lodge, we go for an afternoon boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel (approx. 2 hours) to spot hippos, great herds of buffalo, and diverse water birds.

itinerary.title: Game Drive & Transfer to Ishasha Sector
itinerary.description: A second early morning Kasenyi game drive. Stop for a packed picnic breakfast before driving to the southern Ishasha sector (approx. 2½ hours). Check in and have lunch at the camp. Afternoon game drive searching for the famous tree-climbing lions, large herds of buffaloes, elephants, and Uganda kobs.

itinerary.title: Ishasha Sector to Bwindi Impenetrable NP
itinerary.description: Morning game drive looking out for more animal species like buffaloes, sitatungas, and elephants that cross from Congo. After lunch at the camp, depart to Bwindi Impenetrable NP. The driving time will be between 2 and 3 hours depending on your permitted sector (Buhoma, Rushaga, Nkuringo, or Ruhija).
itinerary.stay: Mahogany Springs Lodge / Lake Mutanda Chameleon Hill Lodge

itinerary.title: Gorilla Trekking in Bwindi
itinerary.description: Breakfast and take a short transfer to Bwindi NP headquarters for a briefing by local guides/rangers and trackers. Hike into the forest with your packed lunch. Trekking can take 1 to 8 hours over rough terrain at high altitudes. Spending 1 hour with the gorillas is an unforgettable and profound natural history experience. Return to the lodge to relax.
itinerary.stay: Mahogany Springs Lodge / Lake Mutanda Chameleon Hill Lodge

itinerary.title: Bwindi to Entebbe & Departure
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, transfer to Entebbe airport (approx. 10-hour journey) stopping along the way for lunch before your evening departure flight.

title: 11 Days Classic Uganda Safari
highlights: Queen Elizabeth game drives & Kazinga boat cruise
Walking safari in Lake Mburo National Park

details.accommodation: Kibale Forest Camp, Mazike Valley Lodge, Arcadia Cottages, Mihingo Lodge

itinerary.title: Arrival in Entebbe
itinerary.description: Arrival at Entebbe, meet and greet. Transfer from the airport to your accommodation in Entebbe.
itinerary.stay: Laico Lake Victoria Hotel / Karibu Guest House

itinerary.title: Transfer to Kibale National Park via Fort Portal
itinerary.description: Start the journey towards Fort Portal. This small town lies in the shadow of the legendary "Moon Mountains", the Rwenzori Mountains. Lunch in Fort Portal and there’s a chance to visit the local market. During the afternoon we arrive in Kibale National Park, a large forest area. There you will stay in the Kibale Forest Camp in the middle of the forest. Around the camp there is a small footpath on which you can go alone on monkey search. With a little luck, you will see 3 different monkey species and possibly the great blue turaco.

itinerary.title: Chimpanzee Tracking & Bigodi Swamp Walk
itinerary.description: Early in the morning we head to the jungle to find chimpanzees. Watching our closest relatives in their natural habitat is a fantastic experience. Afternoon time is for relaxation or you can go on a walk in the Bigodi swamp where there are other chances to see the different species of monkeys. Kibale forest is known for it’s primates with 13 primate species, it is the most primate species rich in Africa. Overnight again at the Kibale Forest Camp.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Queen Elizabeth National Park
itinerary.description: In the morning drive towards Fort Portal, and then along the mystical Rwenzori Mountains towards Queen Elizabeth National Park. Already on the way there is the chance to see elephants, lions, buffalos, hyenas and a variety of antelopes. Lunch on the way or at the lodge in Queen Elizabeth National Park. The afternoon is at your disposal to enjoy the view and perhaps to observe the animals coming near the lodge.
itinerary.stay: Mazike Valley Lodge / Buffalo Safari Lodge

itinerary.title: Morning Game Drive & Kazinga Channel Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: We start our day quite early with a coffee or tea before we embark on a morning game drive in the park. Queen Elizabeth National Park is a diverse ecosystem of savannahs, tropical forests, rivers, swamps, lakes and volcanic craters. It is home to an incredible variety of wildlife. Safaris in this park offer excellent chances to see lions, warthogs, leopards, giant forest hogs, buffaloes, elephants, waterbucks, Uganda kob, topi, bushbucks and other animals. There are over 550 species of birds in the park. In the afternoon, enjoy a one-of-a-kind 2-hour boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel to Lake Edward. This boat tour offers excellent opportunities to see a variety of big game and birds. Dinner and overnight again in the lodge in the park.

itinerary.title: Ishasha Sector (Tree-climbing Lions) to Bwindi Forest
itinerary.description: Today we leave to Bwindi, the drive takes us through the Ishasha Sector of Queen Elizabeth National Park and there we embark on a safari in search of tree-climbing lions and other wildlife. Then continue towards Bwindi Impenetrable National Park. On the way if time allows, we visit Deo's Model Homestead, a local farmer who will show how he protects his fields against elephants on the edge of Queen Elizabeth National Park. Also a stop at Agartha's Taste of Uganda should not be missed. Agartha takes you to the local cuisine of the Bakiga, a local strain, while you can also enjoy the cooked food and then continue to Bwindi, where you will spend the night overlooking the gorilla forest.

itinerary.title: Mountain Gorilla Trekking in Bwindi
itinerary.description: In the early morning, we head to the sanctuary of mountain gorillas, the spectacular Bwindi Impenetrable rainforest. It offers a dramatic, steeply wooded landscape with numerous mammals like the endangered mountain gorillas, the golden monkey, forest elephants, Buffalos, duikers, bushbucks, leopards and giant forest hogs. Meeting the mountain gorillas is an exciting and fascinating experience that you will never forget. Dinner and overnight again in the lodge.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Lake Bunyonyi (Switzerland of Africa)
itinerary.description: After breakfast, we leave the home of the gorillas and through the Kigezi Highlands, an area named by Winston Churchill as the "Switzerland of Africa". After a few hours you will reach Lake Bunyonyi. The property is situated on a hill with excellent views over the many islands of Bunyonyi Lake. Lake Bunyonyi is one of the deepest lakes in the world at a depth of 900 meters. Here there is the possibility to rent a dugout or to go swimming in the lake without danger. Over night and dinner at Arcadia Cottages.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Lake Mburo National Park
itinerary.description: After breakfast drive we to Lake Mburo National Park which is on the way back to Entebbe. In the park you have the chance to see the largest antelope, the Eland antelope, as well as zebras that are found only here and in Kidepo National Park in Uganda. Overnight and dinner at Mihingo Lodge.

itinerary.title: Foot Safari & Optional Horseback Riding
itinerary.description: Early in the morning, we go on a foot safari (optional) and get close to the animals. On this walk you also get close to the famous Ankole Long Horned Cattle. Optionally you could also have the opportunity to go on a horse back riding safari with the lodge or just stay and enjoy the lodge. Our drivers are also available once more for a safari in the park. Overnight and dinner at Mihingo Lodge.

itinerary.title: Equator Stop & Return to Entebbe
itinerary.description: In the morning you have time again to enjoy the lodge depending on your departure flight time. If it’s a late flight, we could take a self guided walk down to the waterhole. After a late breakfast, you will leave Lake Mburo National Park back to Entebbe. This trip brings us back across the equator where we shall stop for lunch and take a souvenir photo if you wish. There after transfer to Entebbe airport for your departure flight.

exclusions: Optional horseback riding in Lake Mburo

itinerary.description: Your honeymoon safari begins with a warm welcome from your private driver/guide at your hotel in Entebbe or Kampala. Depart at 7:00 am for the scenic 5–6 hour drive westward to Queen Elizabeth National Park. Stop at the Uganda Equator monument at Kayabwe for your first memorable photograph. Continue through Mbarara and the Ankole cattle heartland before descending into the Rift Valley. Check in to your luxury lodge — your private cottage or suite has been prepared with flowers, rose petals, chilled champagne and a welcome card. Enjoy a private late afternoon game drive along the Mweya Peninsula, offering exceptional wildlife viewing with the Rwenzori Mountains as a backdrop. Conclude the day with a private honeymoon dinner overlooking the channel.

itinerary.title: PRIVATE GAME DRIVE – KAZINGA CHANNEL PRIVATE BOAT CRUISE – TRANSFER TO BWINDI
itinerary.description: Rise before dawn for a private 4x4 game drive across the Kasenyi Plains. Return for a full breakfast on the terrace before your private boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel — exclusively for two, with an optional on-water picnic. After lunch, drive southward through the Ishasha sector to search for the famous tree-climbing lions. Continue through the dramatic Kigezi highlands to Bwindi Impenetrable Forest. Check in to your luxury forest lodge where a private suite with fireplace awaits you.

itinerary.title: BWINDI IMPENETRABLE FOREST – MOUNTAIN GORILLA TREKKING – FOREST CELEBRATION DINNER
itinerary.description: The day you will never forget. Enter Bwindi Impenetrable Forest for an unhurried hour with a habituated mountain gorilla family. Standing hand-in-hand in the ancient rainforest as gorillas move just metres away is a profound experience. Receive your gorilla trekking completion certificates before returning to the lodge for a late lunch. The afternoon is yours to relax or enjoy a couple's spa treatment. In the evening, enjoy a private candlelit celebration dinner arranged in the forest garden or on your cottage veranda.

itinerary.title: LAKE BUNYONYI – SUNRISE CANOE – ISLAND PICNIC – RETURN TO ENTEBBE/KAMPALA
itinerary.description: Drive to Lake Bunyonyi, the ideal conclusion to your honeymoon. Enjoy a private traditional wooden canoe paddle across the glass-calm water. Bunyonyi is bilharzia-free and safe for swimming — dive in together for a liberating experience. Your boatman will paddle you to a quiet island cove for a private lakeside picnic. After a final lunch on the lake terrace, begin the return journey to Kampala or Entebbe for your departure flight.

itinerary.title: KAMPALA/ENTEBBE – EQUATOR – IGONGO CULTURAL CENTRE – KABALE – LAKE BUNYONYI
itinerary.description: Depart at 7:00 am for a scenic 7–8 hour drive southwestward. Pass through rolling hills and banana groves before climbing into the spectacular Kigezi highlands, popularly known as the 'Switzerland of Africa'. Stop at the Equator for photographs and a water-flow demonstration. Continue to Mbarara for lunch at the Igongo Cultural Centre, exploring the history of the Ankole kingdom and the sacred Bagyendanwa royal drum. Reach Kabale—Uganda's highest town at 1,869 metres—before descending to Lake Bunyonyi (1,962m). Spanning 25km and plunging to depths of 900m, Bunyonyi is Africa's second deepest lake and is entirely free of crocodiles, hippos, and bilharzia. Transfer by motorboat to your lodge for a sunset drink overlooking the 29 islands.
itinerary.stay: Arcadia Cottages / Birdnest at Bunyonyi Resort (Luxury) / Bunyonyi Safaris Resort (Mid-range) / Bushara Island Camp (Budget)

itinerary.title: ISLAND HOPPING – CANOE & BOAT CRUISE – BATWA & BAKIGA CULTURAL VISIT
itinerary.description: Wake to the sound of birdsong and mist rising off the lake. Set out on a guided tour of the lake's storied islands. Visit Akampene (Punishment Island), where unmarried pregnant girls were historically exiled. Explore Bwama Island, home to a leprosy rehabilitation centre established in 1921. Visit Njuyeera Island and Bushara Island for birding (over 200 species recorded). In the afternoon, hike to a Batwa community settlement and a Bakiga homestead. Learn about the extraordinary terracing skills of the Bakiga, sample Ekitooke (banana beer), and listen to ancient folk stories around the fire. This is community tourism at its most authentic and rewarding.
itinerary.stay: Arcadia Cottages / Birdnest at Bunyonyi Resort / Bunyonyi Safaris Resort / Bushara Island Camp

itinerary.title: SUNRISE PADDLE – NATURE WALK – HILLTOP VIEWPOINT – RETURN TO KAMPALA/ENTEBBE
itinerary.description: Rise early for a sunrise canoe paddle across the glassy water—a peaceful highlight for many visitors. After a full cooked breakfast on the terrace, take a nature walk to spot kingfishers, weavers, and sunbirds. Climb to a hilltop viewpoint for a final panoramic view of the 29 islands spread across the shimmering water. Optional visit to the Abaheesi blacksmith community to see traditional iron smelting. Depart in the late morning, stopping at the Kabale weekly market and the Equator for final photos before arriving in Kampala or Entebbe in the early evening.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Entebbe / Kampala
itinerary.description: Arrival at Entebbe airport, meet and greet. Transfer (approximately 30 minutes) to the hotel in the outskirts of Kampala overlooking Lake Victoria. No meals included today.

itinerary.title: Ziwa Rhino Tracking & Transfer to Murchison Falls
itinerary.description: Early breakfast, then depart to Nakitoma to Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary. Game walk to track the white rhinos that are spending the hot hours mostly in the swampy areas. Proceed to Masindi for lunch at Court View Hotel. Continue to Murchison Falls National Park driving through a beautiful landscape that gets flat towards the north near the Victoria Nile. Check in and relax.

itinerary.title: Game Drive & Boat Cruise to the Bottom of Murchison Falls
itinerary.description: Morning game drive on the northern bank of the Nile looking out for elephants, lions, Cape buffalo, Rothschild's giraffe, hartebeest, Oribi, bushbuck, Bohor reedbuck, spotted hyena, and leopards. Back to the lodge for lunch. In the afternoon, a boat cruise upstream to the 'bottom of the falls', stopping near the 'Devil's Cauldron'. Marvel at hippos, crocodiles, and water birds like the Goliath heron, kingfisher, and the rare shoebill stork. Disembark and hike to the 'top of the falls' for a close view of the thunderous waterfall. Driver picks you up from the top (1½ hours transfer back).

itinerary.title: Drive from Murchison Falls to Fort Portal
itinerary.description: Drive to Fort Portal via Hoima in the breathtaking landscape of the Albertine Western Rift Valley. It is a long drive (8-9 hours) with several stopovers for relaxation and sightseeing past verdant countryside, traditional homesteads, and farms. Enjoy a packed/picnic lunch on the way. Check in and relax.

itinerary.title: Kibale Chimpanzee Tracking & Transfer to Queen Elizabeth NP
itinerary.description: Early transfer to Kibale Forest NP (45 minutes) for a morning of chimpanzee tracking and spotting other primates like L'Hoeste's, red colobus, and grey-cheeked mangabeys. After lunch, proceed to the Peninsula sector of Queen Elizabeth National Park (3½ hours) for an evening game drive around the volcanic craters of Katwe.

itinerary.title: Kasenyi Game Drive & Kazinga Channel Boat Cruise
itinerary.description: Early morning game drive in the Kasenyi area within Queen Elizabeth NP, looking for lions, buffaloes, elephants, and large numbers of Uganda Kobs. Lunch at Mweya Safari Lodge. In the afternoon, embark on a 2-hour boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel to spot hippos, great herds of buffalo, and diverse water birds.

itinerary.title: Game Drive & Transfer to Ishasha Sector
itinerary.description: A second early morning Kasenyi game drive. Stop for a packed picnic breakfast, then drive to the southern Ishasha sector (2½ hours). Check in and have lunch at the camp. Afternoon game drive searching for the famous tree-climbing lions, large herds of buffaloes, elephants, and Uganda kobs.

itinerary.title: Ishasha Sector - Tree-climbing Lions
itinerary.description: Morning game drive looking for birds, buffaloes, sitatungas, and elephants that cross from Congo, as well as lions. After lunch and relaxation, take a second afternoon game drive for more chances to observe tree-climbing lions and other magnificent game.

itinerary.title: Ishasha to Volcanoes NP, Rwanda via Cyanika
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, depart for Volcanoes NP in Rwanda (9-10 hours). Cross the Kigezi mountains ('Switzerland of Africa') and Kisoro, stopping for lunch at Traveller's Rest—where Dian Fossey once stayed. Proceed to the Cyanika border post. After clearing immigration, continue to Ruhengeri and Kinigi at the base of the Virunga Volcanoes.

itinerary.title: Gorilla Trekking in Volcanoes National Park
itinerary.description: Take a short drive to the Park Headquarters for etiquette briefing. Hike into the forest to track one of the 10 habituated gorilla groups. Spending 1 hour with these incredible creatures is a profound natural history experience. Return to the lodge for lunch and a free afternoon to relax.

itinerary.title: Return to Kigali & Departure
itinerary.description: Early breakfast before departing to Kigali (2½ hours drive). Depending on flight schedules, visit the Genocide Memorial and a crafts village for souvenir shopping. Transfer to Kigali international airport for your departure.
